A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, and appendices A–F are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations and experiments on Gaussian mixtures, imbalanced image datasets, subgroup robustness benchmarks, and TinyStories, with additional results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds experiments on mixed language/arithmetic data, momentum dynamics, and nonlinear spectral learning.

M1.justification: The SpecGD update and cited practical optimizer implementations are retained. Table 1 and Appendix A clarify optimizer relationships and correct momentum notation, without establishing a change to the implemented algorithms. New model configurations serve additional evaluations.

E1.justification: New Appendix D.7 introduces domain imbalance through a TinyStories/add-k mixture, requiring arithmetic prediction from example input–output pairs alongside language modeling. This substantially extends task coverage to minority skill acquisition; the earlier datasets remain.

E2.justification: Appendix C, Figure 10 adds Adam and Muon to the existing GD, NGD, SignGD, and SpecGD comparison. New Figure 12 also compares Muon with theoretical and empirical SpecGD dynamics. These are localized comparator additions; the retained benchmark comparator sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce substantive evaluation designs: D.7 uses 18,000 narrative and 2,000 arithmetic training samples, 500 held-out samples per domain, and arithmetic exact-match accuracy. D.10 introduces KL divergence between uniform and normalized logit singular values, with a fixed-readout nonlinear Gaussian experiment and analysis of retained CIFAR settings. These supplement rather than replace existing protocols.

E4.justification: Appendix C extends the dynamics analysis to momentum-based Muon under population and finite-sample conditions. New D.10 directly examines spectral balance in nonlinear models trained with cross-entropy, using Gaussian mixtures and CIFAR-10. These materially extend the mechanism tests beyond the earlier linear analyses; the existing diagonalizability perturbation test is retained.

E5.justification: Retained experiments keep their existing repeated-run reporting, including three runs for MNIST-CIFAR, four for MultiNLI, and five for Colored-MNIST and CelebA. The new Gaussian analysis likewise averages five seeds, continuing the existing practice rather than introducing a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds Adam/Muon trajectories in Figure 10, finite-sample Muon–SpecGD agreement in Figure 12, and arithmetic results in Figure 28 showing Muon and Adam outperforming SGD on the minority task. Figures 31–32 add nonlinear spectral-balance findings. Existing benchmark results are retained; the new results do not establish improved performance over v1 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: v2 corrects Lemma 3.1 from syx_c = p_c to syx_c = mu p_c, repairs the max-norm definition, and adds explicit step-size restrictions. It removes the limiting-initialization qualification from Proposition 3 and supplies a derivation of Shampoo's reduction to SpecGD. The central loss-gap theorems and most proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions retain the same claims about balanced spectral learning, early generalization advantages over GD/NGD, and depth effects. The added experiments support these claims without redefining the paper's core contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds a practical rationale for joint diagonalizability and extends the balanced-learning interpretation to nonlinear logit spectra and minority arithmetic skills. Appendix F's limitations remain unchanged. Figure 32's new caption overstates the evidence by claiming lower divergence throughout training, although Signum falls below Muon late in training.

D1.justification: The added experiments document arithmetic sequence construction, mixture sizes, transformer reuse, training budgets, and optimizer hyperparameters. Appendix C supplies settings for the additional Muon comparisons, and D.10 supplies Gaussian sample counts and learning rates. Existing implementation references and access information are retained.

R1.justification: The bibliography and related-work section are substantively retained. Section 3.2 adds a focused discussion of the already-cited Gidel et al. work, using its approximate joint-diagonalizability findings on practical datasets to motivate the paper's stricter analytical assumption.

P1.justification: v2 adds an optimizer overview, expands explanations around assumptions and dynamics, and inserts two experimental appendix subsections. Terminology and several sentences are corrected, while the overall narrative and section ordering remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the optimizer-summary Table 1 and new Figures 12, 28, 31, and 32 covering dynamics, arithmetic performance, and nonlinear spectral diagnostics. Figure 10 is enlarged and extended with comparator curves and legends. Other figures retain their contents, with relocation and renumbering rather than replacement.

improvement.justification: The added momentum and nonlinear spectral analyses strengthen the empirical connection between the simplified theory and practical optimizers. The optimizer overview and mathematical corrections also improve clarity. The gains remain limited by the unchanged theoretical scope, and Figure 32's claim of an advantage throughout training overstates its plotted comparison with Signum.
